prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” dentist for implants that fits everyone — the right provider depends on your case (single tooth vs full-arch), location, budget, insurance, and whether you prefer a specialist. I can help you find the best option in Miami if you tell me your ZIP code and a few preferences. Meanwhile, here’s how to find a top implant provider and what to look for.

Which specialist to consider
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeon — best for surgical complexity (bone grafts, extractions, full-arch, sedation).
- Periodontist — specializes in gums and implants; excellent for esthetic or peri-implant tissue concerns.
- Prosthodontist — specializes in restoring teeth; ideal if the final crown/bridge/overdenture fit/esthetics are critical.
- Some general dentists place implants and restore them; look for additional implant training/certifications.

What to look for
- Training & credentials: board certification or membership in AAOMS, AAP, ACP, or implant fellowships.
- Experience: number/type of implants placed per year and specific experience with your procedure (single tooth, multiple implants, All‑on‑4).
- Technology: in‑office CBCT (3D imaging), guided surgery, digital planning, CAD/CAM restorations.
- Before/after photos and patient references or reviews.
- Collaborative care: a team approach (surgeon + prosthodontist) for complex cases.
- Guarantee/warranty, follow‑up plan, and emergency availability.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many implants like mine have you done? Success rate/complications?
- Which implant system do you use and why?
- Will I need bone grafts or sinus lifts? How long will the process take?
- Can I see before/after photos of similar cases and speak with past patients?
- Who will do the surgical placement and who will make the crown?
- What are total fees and what’s included (surgery, imaging, temporary restoration, final restoration)?
- What sedation options and aftercare do you provide?

Red flags
- No before/after photos or references.
- Pressure to accept a one‑visit “implant & crown” without proper planning.
- Vague answers about experience or implant brand.
- Extremely low price without clear explanation.

Where to search
- AAOMS (oral surgeons), AAP (periodontists), ACP (prosthodontists) “find a specialist” directories.
- Google/Healthgrades/Yelp/RealSelf reviews and Zocdoc for appointment availability.
- Florida State Board of Dentistry for license and disciplinary history.

If you want, give me your Miami ZIP code, whether it’s a single tooth or full-arch, and if you have any insurance preferences — I can suggest highly rated implant specialists/clinics in your area and help you compare them.
